title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
reason: As a student juggling law studies and a deep curiosity about how societies and structures came to be, Sapiens strikes me as exactly the kind of book that connects big-picture human history to the systems I encounter in both law and engineering. Harari's work is well-known for being accessible yet intellectually rigorous, which suits my reading style perfectly. The fact that it has a perfect five-star rating on the catalog only confirms what I already suspected: this is a book worth investing in, even at a higher price point. It directly feeds my achievement drive and my need to understand the world at a macro level before diving into the specifics of any single discipline.
